title: I had Claude generate the trailer for this game.
author: spikyness27
selftext: This was completed during commute prompting during the day today with opus and Godot.

replies.author: spikyness27
replies.body:
Many to get to this point believe it or now. Today was getting opus to create the trailer. I saw the other guys star Fox clone and it looks amazing. 

But essentially today was getting Claude to build a trailer for this game. Show off the various worlds with increasing difficulty, show off the map, level ups after each level and bosses. Since go dot has a mode for filming essentially it was able to setup a script for the level generations and recording. 

I'm still working on mechanics for the most part. Enumerating gameplay mechanics with this format is interesting.

replies.author: joeban1
replies.body: Yeah so what was the prompt for it to create a trailer

replies.author: spikyness27
replies.body: are you able to create a seperate branch and I would like you to make me a trailer for the game. trailer needs to be 60fps. have some in game music. show off multiple levels. bosses in multiple cuts back to back. show persistent mods for the ship plus level ups after each level and the game map. can you give me a written narrative of how this will look before you put it all together

replies.author: redPistolStar
replies.body: Well how exactly did you build the trailer is what I am asking. I tried building one for my game but it didn't come out right

replies.author: spikyness27
replies.body:
I think that came from one of my rules when building the game is to have a test build framework where you can play through the game and track stats and analytics. If I'm not testing the game it's gathering analytics on its progress that I then use to balance the game. 

To make the video it modified this framework and got some video capture. From the start it's been built to have an AI play through, capture screenshots review screen shots for clipping and bugs and to create a list that is then corrected later.

comments.author: BrotherMoy
comments.body: What MCP do you used for Godot?

replies.author: spikyness27
replies.body: I create a project tell Claude it's a godot project and tell it to have at it. No MCP involved. Godot has implemented quite a few features to be AI friendly and since the source code is open sources Claude has likely trained against the source code.

replies.author: BrotherMoy
replies.body: Wow that's crazy, how much interference do you have to do? I thought Claude had no context to what a node is or scene file, so it can't directly edit some things

replies.author: BoredzzzGame
replies.body: Just use Claude code and point it to your godot project folder or it can start from scratch and create it for you. I run Claude in terminal but pretty sure the desktop app works the same. I also run bypassing permissions.

comments.author: BoredzzzGame
comments.body: Pretty fugging cool. What’s your pipeline going to be like when you replace the Godot assets? which btw I think is pretty cool…like a more stylish gray box

replies.author: spikyness27
replies.body:
Looking at the assets needing to be fixed first is the wrong angle. Lighting is the first place to start, adding fog and bloom. We want to keep still retro but elevate it. 

Since AI is being heavily used in the project. I'm going and generating a more "realistic" image using AI slop. Then requesting AI to plan and then iterate to get closer to the look of the higher realizm image. Once that's done I'm going to start building some assets but still keep it on the retro theme
